'''Weygand''': {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Lincoln Chafee]]{{efn|In October 1999, Chafee was appointed by Governor [[Lincoln Almond]] to fill the vacancy caused by the death of (his father) Senator [[John Chafee]].}} | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Lincoln Chafee]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsRI}} The '''2000 United States Senate election in Rhode Island''' was held on November 7, 2000. Republican incumbent [[Lincoln Chafee]], who had been appointed to his late father, won re-election over Democratic congressman [[Robert Weygand]]. {{As of|2026}}, this is the last Rhode Island congressional election won by a Republican. == Background == At a state and federal level, Rhode Island has been one of the most Democratic states in the country since the [[1930s]]. Nonetheless, Republican senator [[John Chafee]] managed to continually win re-election as a moderate Republican. Republican senator [[John Chafee]] announced in 1999 that he would not seek reelection to a fifth term in office, leading his son, [[Warwick, Rhode Island|Warwick]] mayor [[Lincoln Chafee]], to announce his own candidacy for the seat. John Chafee died in October 1999, leaving the seat vacant.
